messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak landed I’m seeing a regression on A10 for long-context workloads. p95 up ~12% when avg request ~450 tokens.

aj: Huh, did we change max_tokens_per_batch or max_batch_count in the same PR?

maria: No, I only touched kernel selection heuristics; but looked at traces and batch formation looks different — more smaller batches rather than a few medium ones.

kevin: Can you paste the profiler snippet? I want to check KV cache misses vs kernel switch points.

maria: pasted logs: ```
[trace] model=redwood-l2, gpu=A10, run=2026-03-16T08:12:21Z
batch_sizes: [1,1,2,3,1,4,1,2]
max_tokens_per_batch=4096
observed_tokens_per_batch= [300, 120, 620, 980, 140, 1500, 90, 400]
kernel_selector: kernel_selector_v2 -> fallback kernel_fused_attn at token=512
kv_cache_hits_ratio: 0.68 -> 0.47 after selector change
latency_p95: baseline=210ms, current=235ms
```

samir: Observed the same pattern in the T4 cluster yesterday — more tiny batches for requests with variable lengths. We tuned queue timeout to 6ms and it improved batching a bit.

aj: Important to correlate `kernel switching` boundaries with `batch token envelope` — if selector switches at certain seq_len, it can split continuous batches prematurely.

kevin: Agreed. Hypothesis: new selector chooses smaller-kernel for short sequences; but when heterogeneous seq lengths queue policy forms batches by arrival not by token budget, so short+long mix triggers frequent kernel changes and KV cache thrash.

maria: Proposed quick mitigations: 1) introduce per-GPU soft cap on `max_tokens_per_batch` that biases batching to prefer filling token budget before dispatch for A10/T4/L4, 2) increase `batch_wait_ms` by 2ms for queues with >25% short requests, 3) add kernel-selection hysteresis (avoid switching kernels within first N tokens of a batch).

aj: Can we try soft caps: A100=8192, H100=16384, A10=4096->5120, T4=3072->3584, L4=4096? Keep as soft (will break if latency SLOs violated).

kevin: I’ll run a quick experiment on canary: set A10 max_tokens_per_batch=5120 and enable kernel hysteresis=256 tokens, run 2k requests, capture p50/p95 and KV hit ratio.

infra-bot: Started job job-1876543210-canary-1 on cluster eng-runtime-canaries (A10 pool).

maria: Thanks. Also add a profiler flag to capture `kernel_id` per token so we can confirm switches inside a batch: `--trace-kernel-boundaries`.

samir: Dataset I used for T4 test is in s3://redwood-testdata/long-tail-requests/2026-03-15.json — mimic that load.

kevin: Quick results: p95 dropped from 235ms -> 218ms with soft cap + hysteresis, kv_cache_hits_ratio improved 0.47 -> 0.61, median unchanged. No SLA breaches in 30m canary.

maria: Nice. Any regression on A100/H100?

kevin: A100 can avoid soft cap bump; H100 already fine. Will run L4 next.

aj: Next steps: 1) run L4/T4 canaries with same config, 2) bake per-GPU defaults into batcher config (soft caps + hysteresis), 3) add a runtime metric `kernel_switches_per_batch` and alert when >0.5 for a given model & GPU combo.

maria: I’ll open a short RFC with configs and rollout plan. Keep this thread for quick notes. :thumbsup:

kevin: Nice work. If canary on L4/T4 looks good we can rollout to Dedicated pools tomorrow morning.

infra-bot: job job-1876543210-canary-1 completed successfully (30m run).

maria: Filing follow-up: need to add unit tests for `batch formation` under mixed-length arrivals to prevent regressions.

aj: FYI: record of the profiler traces uploaded to internal bucket: s3://redwood-internal/prof/traces/1876543210/

kevin: Will post canary graphs (p50/p95/kv-hit/kernel-switches) in this thread when available.
